clue.text: Maybe a Glaswegian's clothes items

blocks.note: taken as written
a Glaswegian is one example of a Scot, hence 'Maybe'; the possessive gives Scot's

explanation.surface: Some garments that might belong to a man from Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as A SCOT'S and the apostrophe vanishes; 'Maybe' flags that a Glaswegian is just one kind of Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad neckscarf or cravat, so ascots are items of clothing.

clue.text: A British Queen deemed good person for keeping order?

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for British
Elizabeth I was known as Good Queen Bess

explanation.surface: A British monarch, reckoned virtuous, was good at maintaining discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: The order to be kept is a religious one, not public order: hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbess heads a convent of nuns, an order she oversees.

clue.text: Form of silica in earth's crust

indicators.note: a form of a word here means another shape made from its letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A type of silica found in the planet's outer layer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is nearly literal, as sial is rich in silica and alumina.
explanation.definitionFit: Sialic describes sial, the upper layer of the continental crust, so it pertains to the crust.

clue.text: Little credit given to a cruel schoolteacher ("Fish")

blocks.note: CR is the short form of credit
taken as written
a cruel old-style teacher might beat pupils

explanation.surface: A harsh teacher nicknamed Fish gets scant recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'Fish' reads like a nickname but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Crab-eater is another name for the cobia, a large game fish.

clue.text: Manner with which dale changes in region of southern England

indicators.note: a word that changes is altered, its letters rearranged

blocks.note: thew is an old word for manner or custom
taken as written

explanation.surface: The way a valley evolves across part of southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weald is the once-wooded area between the North and South Downs in Kent, Sussex and Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weald is a named district of south-east England.

clue.text: Snake is showing evidence of harmful bacteria

blocks.note: a seps is a kind of snake-like lizard or serpent
taken as written

explanation.surface: A serpent displays signs of a nasty infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepsis is the body's response to infection by harmful microorganisms in tissue or blood.

clue.text: Form of response included by communists making new offers

indicators.note: something included by another is held within it, so one piece goes inside the next

blocks.note: Reds is the usual nickname for communists
in Chambers, bi is a term from Chinese medicine for a kind of bodily response

explanation.surface: A political committee drafts a reply that the communist members must absorb.
explanation.walkthrough: BI is an obscure Chambers word, typical of Mephisto; the definition is the verb phrase at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebid is to bid again, so someone who rebids is putting forward fresh offers, as at auction or in bridge.

clue.text: Sort of sticky boy admitting transgression

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Roy is a boy's name
a sin is a transgression

explanation.surface: A lad owning up to wrongdoing is in a tricky spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosiny means like or full of rosin, the resin that makes things tacky.

clue.text: Area of land no longer British, egg-shaped

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
ovate means egg-shaped

explanation.surface: A plot that has ceased to be British, oddly oval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' looks like it governs British, but it belongs to the definition, marking an obsolete unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bovate was an old measure of land, the area one ox could plough in a year.

clue.text: Demand for justice is religious virtue, any number coming in for mass

indicators.note: one thing coming in for another takes over its place, like a substitute player

blocks.note: dharma is the Hindu and Buddhist idea of righteous conduct
N stands for any number in maths
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A plea for fairness rests on piety, with many people attending Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' suggests a church service, but it is the physics symbol, swapped out for N.
explanation.definitionFit: A dharna is an Indian protest of sitting fasting at a door until a demand for redress is met.

clue.text: Cleaner transforming den ("sty")

indicators.note: transforming something changes its form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleaner is turning a dingy den into a pigsty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is ironic: the cleaner seems to make the room filthier.
explanation.definitionFit: Syndet is short for synthetic detergent, a cleaning agent.

clue.text: System of belief of those people gathering round second-year student

indicators.note: to gather something is to draw it in and hold it, so these letters enclose what follows

blocks.note: they is the pronoun for those people
O is round in shape
soph is short for sophomore, a second-year student

explanation.surface: A creed held by a group who cluster around a sophomore.
explanation.walkthrough: Sophomore, shortened here, is mainly American for a second-year student at college or high school.
explanation.definitionFit: Theosophy is a mystical religious philosophy, so it is a set of beliefs.

clue.text: Bleats of leader in South Africa

blocks.note: first meaning: the cries a sheep makes
second meaning: Afrikaans word for a master or boss

explanation.surface: The complaints voiced by a South African politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The South African word is singular, cognate with boss; the sheep cries are a plural noun spelt the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A baa is a sheep's cry, and baas is the Afrikaans term for a boss or master.

clue.text: Thus small Roman community managed with very old ruler

blocks.note: so means thus
V is the international vehicle code for Vatican City, a tiny state in Rome
ran a business is managed it

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman settlement was governed by an old king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very' belongs to the definition, signalling an archaic word; the small community is Vatican City.
explanation.definitionFit: Sovran is an old poetic spelling of sovereign, a monarch or ruler.

clue.text: Be slow moving joints

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift their positions into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to take it easy when moving one's joints.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the hinge joint in the middle of the arm.

clue.text: Bear without tail seen in copse

indicators.note: having no tail means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: to bear a load is to carry it

explanation.surface: A tailless bear has been spotted among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A carr is a boggy patch of woodland, typically of alder or willow, so a type of copse.

clue.text: Errors yet to be put right by this unruly type

indicators.note: putting something right means rearranging what was wrong into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mistakes still to be corrected by a rowdy person.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that the unruly type is the last person to put errors right.
explanation.definitionFit: A roysterer, or roisterer, is a noisy reveller who behaves in a boisterous way.

clue.text: Rock event is on in new format

indicators.note: putting something into a new format rearranges it, here the letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock concert is going ahead with a fresh line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests music, but it is the geological definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Veinstone is the mineral matter, or gangue, filling a vein of ore, a kind of rock.

clue.text: Combination of nice oils that may enhance the breast

indicators.note: a combination mixes things together, so these letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A blend of pleasant oils marketed as a bust enhancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicone gel is used in implants for cosmetic breast augmentation.

clue.text: Rascal not getting married, one to run away

indicators.note: not getting something means going without it, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a scamp is a rascal
M is the abbreviation for married
a means one

explanation.surface: A rogue avoiding marriage becomes someone keen to bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the married abbreviation from the rascal and add A.
explanation.definitionFit: Scapa is an old slang verb meaning to escape or decamp, so to run off.

clue.text: Abnormal pulse — one admitted medical problem

indicators.note: something abnormal is out of its usual form, so the letters are disordered
something admitted is let inside, so a piece goes within the others

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An irregular heartbeat, with one patient admitted for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a hospital admission; 'admitted' signals I going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An epulis is a benign tumour or swelling on the gum, a medical condition.

clue.text: Electronic device with double power stuffed with lots of paper

indicators.note: a thing stuffed with something holds it inside, so one piece is placed within

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power, doubled
a ream is a large quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A gadget packed with paper that boosts power twofold.
explanation.definitionFit: A preamp, short for preamplifier, boosts a weak signal before the main amplifier.

clue.text: Good old Aussie star

definitions.note: 'old Aussie' marks the sense as dated Australian slang

blocks.note: first meaning: dated Australian slang for fine or excellent
second meaning: one of the twin stars in Gemini

explanation.walkthrough: The surface praises a veteran Australian celebrity; in fact it pairs an old slang word with a star name.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor was old Australian slang for good, and Castor is a bright star in the constellation Gemini.

clue.text: Very short relation being boastful

blocks.note: V is the short form of very
an aunty is a relation

explanation.surface: A rather small relative showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very short' looks like a description of the relation, but it means V.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaunty is a Scots and dialect adjective meaning proud or bragging, from vaunt.

clue.text: Old mother with problem in stomach

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
ma is a familiar word for mother
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: An elderly mum has a tummy complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The omasum is the third compartment of a ruminant's stomach.

clue.text: The Parisian unwell, about to avoid that surgical procedure

indicators.note: something made to avoid a letter goes without it, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: la is French for 'the' (feminine)
sick means unwell
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman feeling ill hopes to dodge an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: Circa, abbreviated C, is the Latin for about, used with dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasik is laser eye surgery to correct vision, an operation on the cornea.

clue.text: Natural troublemaker undermining place of hospitality

blocks.note: an inn offers food and lodging
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A born rabble-rouser causing trouble at a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'undermining' simply places the troublemaker beneath the inn, so the pieces are read top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate means inborn, present from birth rather than learned.

clue.text: On outside of fish insect turned up

indicators.note: being on the outside of something means wrapping round it

blocks.note: a ked is a sheep tick, a wingless fly
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A bug found clinging to a fish has flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like 'arrived', but it means upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To keel, or keel over, is to capsize, so keeled means turned bottom up.

clue.text: Trained paramedic appearing before man in garden?

indicators.note: something trained has been shaped and drilled into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An ambulance worker turns up ahead of a gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: The man in the garden is Adam in Eden; the question mark marks a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-Adamic means existing before Adam, the first man, placed in the Garden of Eden.

clue.text: Part of ruler's territory at one time

indicators.note: a part of a phrase is a stretch of its letters, read straight through

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A section of a monarch's land, once upon a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Erst is an archaic word for formerly, as in erstwhile.

clue.text: Long to eat nut and dry fruit

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one piece is swallowed by another

blocks.note: to ache for is to long for
an en, or nut, is a printing measure

explanation.surface: Yearning to snack on a nut and some dried fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Printers call the en a 'nut' to avoid confusing it with the em, which they call a 'mutton'.
explanation.definitionFit: An achene is a small, dry, one-seeded fruit that does not split open, like a buttercup seed.

clue.text: Old brass pillar with X on

blocks.note: a lat is a type of Indian or Buddhist pillar
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An ancient brass column marked with a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: X looks like a marked cross, but it is the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Latten is a yellow alloy like brass, used in the past for church fittings.

clue.text: Poisonous plant mostly seen in river

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: urali, also called curare, is a poisonous plant extract

explanation.surface: A toxic weed has been spotted growing in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word; the Ural flows from the Ural Mountains to the Caspian Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural is a major river in Russia and Kazakhstan.

clue.text: This writer's left with a French female creating torment

blocks.note: this writer is the setter, I; 'This writer's' is I'm, I am
port is the left side of a ship
une is the feminine form of 'a' in French

explanation.surface: An author abandoned by a Frenchwoman is in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb, but it is the nautical side.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune originally meant to trouble or harass persistently, hence to torment.

clue.text: Like crystal box rarely empty

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: to spar is to box
only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: A crystal casket is seldom left vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like a container, but it is the verb for fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Spar is a glassy crystalline mineral, so sparry means resembling or containing crystals.

clue.text: Like poetry that's encountered, set in good order

blocks.note: met means encountered
red, also spelt redd, is a dialect verb meaning to tidy up

explanation.surface: Verse one comes across, arranged neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: Red here is not the colour but a Scots and dialect verb for tidying.
explanation.definitionFit: Metred verse has a regular rhythmic pattern of stresses, as much poetry does.
